questions.text: Which of the following security principles is primarily violated if data integrity is compromised but confidentiality and availability are intact?
In the CIA triad, which security property ensures that information is accessible to authorized users when needed and is most vulnerable to Denial of Service (DoS) attacks?
Which cryptographic property directly supports data integrity by allowing verification that data has not been altered?
Which of the following scenarios represents a breach of confidentiality?
options: An attacker deletes critical files, making them unavailable
An attacker reads sensitive information without permission
Data backup failure causes loss of data availability

questions.text: Which type of attack targets the ‘availability’ aspect of the CIA triad by flooding the target system with excessive requests?
Which of the following would best compromise the availability of an organization's data?
Which of the following best describes the primary ethical distinction between white hat and gray hat hackers?
options: A) Gray hats always operate under legal contracts
B) White hats exploit zero-days for monetary gain
C) White hats operate with prior authorization; gray hats do not
D) Gray hats never report discovered vulnerabilities

questions.text: Which hacker type is most likely to submit vulnerability findings to a company’s public bug bounty program?

A hacker bypasses authentication on a public-facing server and reports the vulnerability to the organization, requesting a reward. The organization has no responsible disclosure policy. This hacker is best categorized as:
Which of the following actions is LEAST likely to be performed by a black hat hacker?
options: A) Sell stolen credentials on dark web forums
B) Perform penetration testing under a signed NDA
C) Deploy ransomware to extort payment
D) Use phishing to gain unauthorized access

questions.text: Which scenario most closely represents gray hat behavior?
options: A) Reporting a bug via a company’s official disclosure program
B) Selling a zero-day exploit to a cybercrime syndicate
C) Launching a DDoS attack to protest censorship
D) Gaining unauthorized access to a system and later informing the owner

questions.text: Which factor is most critical in legally distinguishing ethical hacking from cybercrime?
Which of the following scenarios represents a blend of both passive and active reconnaissance?
options: A) Monitoring a company's job postings for tech stack info
B) Using Shodan to identify IoT devices and confirming responses via Telnet
C) Running an Nmap SYN scan on all subnets
D) Searching for default credentials in leaked credential dumps

questions.text: Which tactic is typically used to ensure access remains available even after a reboot or patch is applied?
options: C) Creating a startup registry key for a RAT
D) Running a SYN flood on a service

questions.text: Which of the following best describes a key operational difference between Reconnaissance and Scanning?
options: A) Reconnaissance uses only automated tools; scanning does not
B) Scanning involves interaction with the target system, while reconnaissance may not
C) Reconnaissance requires credentials; scanning does not
D) Scanning is completely stealthy; reconnaissance is always detected

questions.text: Which of the following is a primary objective of banner grabbing?
options: B) Identify OS and service versions

questions.text: Which scanning type involves the use of ICMP Echo Requests and no TCP communication?
After gaining shell access to a Linux system via a misconfigured cron job, what’s the next logical step in this phase?
In Black Box Testing, which of the following best mimics a real-world external attack scenario?
options: A) Access to API documentation and credentials
B) Use of fuzzing against known components
C) Injection testing using debug logs

questions.text: Gray Box Testing allows testers to focus on which key area?
options: D) Privilege escalation across trust zones

questions.text: Which statement is TRUE regarding White Box Testing in penetration testing?
options: A) It is blind and mirrors an unprivileged user
B) It cannot identify race conditions
C) It focuses only on network penetration
D) It involves complete transparency and internal access

questions.text: Which of the following is most often omitted in Black Box Testing?
In which testing model is the tester likely unaware of IP ranges, software stacks, and authentication methods?
Which vulnerability type is best discovered through manual code inspection in White Box testing?
What is the PRIMARY goal of the exploitation phase in a pentest?
options: D) Verify real-world impact of vulnerabilities
